title: Q2 Playbook: SLO-first Capacity Cadence & Autoscale Experiment Runway
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Objective: Create a repeatable quarterly cadence that ties Dedicated pool reservations and autoscale policies directly to SLO bands. Deliver a lightweight experiment runway so platform, infra, and product teams can run controlled autoscale pilots with clear success criteria and rollback paths. This playbook will reduce late-cycle firefighting, improve cost predictability, and surface failure modes earlier in the experiment lifecycle.

Scope: Focused on Dedicated capacity only for Q2 pilot:
- Define three SLO bands (Gold/Silver/Bronze) and corresponding pre-warm + autoscale parameters.
- Build an experiment template (traffic shaping, canary windows, metric dashboards, alerting).
- Implement a read-only dashboard slice in Console for experiment owners to track cost/latency/QoE.
- Create an ops runbook for canary-to-rollout transitions and emergency fallback to hosted model variants.

Out of scope: Billing model changes, full Dedicated product pricing updates, VPC-specific networking changes beyond access controls.
background: Repeated Q1 incidents where late capacity decisions caused either cost spikes or throttled customer traffic.
Current reserved pool policy is decoupled from SLO tiers; teams operate reactive top-ups rather than SLO-driven capacity decisions.
Platform teams have experimented with autoscale but lack standardized experiment templates and rollback criteria across regions and model families.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible experiment template exists that can be executed by any Dedicated customer or internal team within the Console.
Three SLO bands are documented with concrete autoscale policy defaults (min_prewarm, burst_threshold, cooldown_seconds).
Dashboard tile in Console shows token-cost, P50/P95/P99 latency, autoscale events, and canary window annotations for any running experiment.
Playbook includes step-by-step canary and rollback procedures and a post-run checklist with learning capture fields.
Two internal pilot runs completed (one small-scale, one region+model variant) with documented metrics and a retro.
work_items: Define SLO bands and map to autoscale policy knobs (PM + SRE)
Design experiment template and traffic shaping recipe (Product + Eng)
Build Console dashboard tile and experiment UI surface (Console UX + Frontend)
Instrumentation: ensure autoscale events, model fallbacks, and cost attribution are emitted to tracing and metrics (Infra)
Run two pilots and collect postmortems (PM owns coordination)
Write final playbook doc, checklist, and handoff to Operations
metrics_and_targets: P99 end-to-end inference latency for Gold SLO <= 180ms during normal load
Autoscale action success rate >= 98% (defined as capacity delta applied and effective within configured cooldown)
Experiment cost variance vs baseline <= +12% for initial canary (goal: < +5% in steady runs)
Time-to-detect degrading QoE via alerting <= 5 minutes
Post-run regression rate (quality) <= 1% compared to baseline prompt set

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Autoscale policy causes oscillation under bursty workloads. Mitigation: enforce minimum cooldown and add hysteresis rules; run synthetic burst tests before rollouts.
Risk: Console dashboard does not surface root cause fast enough. Mitigation: include annotated traces and quick links to recent autoscale events; add playbook checklist for triage.
Risk: Pilot increases cost beyond acceptable threshold. Mitigation: cap pilot burst capacity and enable automatic rollback on cost threshold breach.
